# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 29 HUGH AND NELL DISAGREE

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Hugh set aside the heavy medical book he had been reading closely until the growing darkness of the March twilight forced him to stop. Resting back in his seat, he looked out the window in a thoughtful mood. Early spring had arrived, which was likely the most unpleasant season of all. The gloomy, waterlogged countryside and decaying, dark ice in the harbor that met his gaze could not be saved even by the setting sun. Except for a large black crow flying alone over a grey field, no living thing could be seen. Hugh found himself idly wondering about the bird. Was it a family-oriented crow, headed toward a dark yet attractive crow mate waiting in the forest past the Glen? Was it perhaps a sleek young male crow whose mind was set on romance? Or could it be a skeptical bachelor crow, holding the view that one travels quickest when journeying unaccompanied? Whichever it might be, the bird shortly vanished into the fitting darkness, causing Hugh to direct his attention to the more inviting scene inside.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0000 }

The light from the hearth danced from place to place, shining upon the white and green jackets of Gog and Magog, upon the smooth, brown skull of the lovely setter resting on the mat, upon the frames of the pictures hanging on the walls, upon the vase packed with daffodils taken from the window garden, upon Nell herself, who was seated beside her small table, having her needlework next to her and her hands locked around her knee as she imagined images within the flames—Castles in Spain with delicate towers that broke through moonlit cloud and sunset bar—vessels journeying out of the Haven of Good Hopes directly toward Seven Gulls Harbor carrying valuable cargo. Because Nell had returned to dreaming dreams, even though a dark figure of dread accompanied her evening and morning to dim and obscure her imaginings.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0001 }

Hugh routinely described himself as “an old married man.” Nevertheless, he continued to gaze at Nell with a lover's disbelieving eyes. That she truly belonged to him was something he was not yet completely able to accept. This entire experience MIGHT simply be a fantasy, inextricably linked to this enchanted house of dreams. Before her, his spirit still proceeded cautiously, afraid that the spell might break and the illusion vanish.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0002 }

“Nell,” he uttered unhurriedly, “listen to me. I need to speak to you concerning a matter.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0003 }

Nell peered over toward him amidst the shadows illuminated by the fire.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0004 }

“What’s the matter?” she inquired lightheartedly. “Hugh, your expression is terribly grave. I assure you I’ve been good all day. Check with Tabitha.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0005 }

“I do not wish to speak regarding you—or about ourselves,” I said. “It concerns Rufus Vane.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0006 }

“Rufus Vane?” repeated Nell, straightening herself with interest. “Why, whatever do you have to tell regarding Rufus Vane?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0007 }

“Lately, my thoughts have been occupied with him quite a bit. That time last summer when I provided treatment for the carbuncles on his neck, do you recall it?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0008 }

“Yes—yes.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0009 }

“I made use of the occasion to meticulously inspect the marks on his scalp. From a clinical perspective, Rufus has continually struck me as quite a fascinating subject. Recently, my research has focused on the background of trephining along with instances in which it was utilized. Nell, my deduction is that should Rufus Vane be brought to a reputable medical facility and undergo trephining across various areas of his head, it could revive his recollections and mental capabilities.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0010 }

“Hugh!” cried Nell, her tone rich with objection. “You cannot possibly be serious!”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0011 }

“I certainly do. Furthermore, I have made up my mind that I am obligated to introduce the topic to Lorna.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0012 }

“You must NOT engage in anything of the sort, Hugh Carrow,” Nell exclaimed passionately. “Oh, Hugh, you will refrain—you will refrain. Such cruelty is beyond you. Give me your word that you will not.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0013 }

“Why, Nell-girl, I never thought you’d react in this manner. Listen to reason—”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0014 }

“I will not be reasonable—I am unable to be reasonable—I AM reasonable. You are the one who is unreasonable. Hugh, have you at any point considered what Lorna would experience if Rufus Vane was returned to his proper mind? Merely halt and consider it! Currently her unhappiness is bad enough; however, existing as the nurse and caregiver for Rufus is a thousand times simpler for her than existing as the wife of Rufus. I know—I KNOW! It cannot be thought of. Do not interfere in this business. Allow what is adequate to remain as it is.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0015 }

“ Nell, I have given exhaustive thought to that side of the matter. However, it is my belief that a physician must place the holiness of a patient's mind and body higher than any other concerns, regardless of the repercussions. It is my conviction that his obligation is to strive to bring back health and sanity, provided any prospect at all remains.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0016 }

“However, Rufus does not belong to you as a patient in that regard,” Nell exclaimed, shifting her approach. “HAD Lorna questioned you about whether he could be helped, IT WOULD BE your obligation to reveal your true opinion to her. You possess no entitlement to interfere, though.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0017 }

“It doesn't seem like meddling to me. A dozen years back, Uncle Dave informed Lorna that Rufus was beyond help. Naturally, she accepts that as truth.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0018 }

“And if it wasn’t true, why did Uncle Dave tell her that?” Nell exclaimed, triumphantly. “Is his knowledge about it any less than yours?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0019 }

“I do not believe so—even if stating this might appear arrogant and self-important. Furthermore, it is just as clear to you as it is to me that he holds a certain bias against what he terms 'these new-fangled notions of cutting and carving.’ He is resistant even to performing surgery for appendicitis.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0020 }

“He is correct,” Nell cried out, altering her position entirely. “Personally, I am convinced that you contemporary physicians are far too eager to test your ideas on living people.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0021 }

“If I had hesitated to perform a particular test, Rhoda Allonby would not be among the living now,” Hugh insisted. “I accepted the danger—and rescued her.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0022 }

“I have had enough of listening to talk regarding Rhoda Allonby,” exclaimed Nell—unfairly in the extreme, because Hugh had not brought up Mrs. Allonby’s name a single time after the day he informed Nell about his triumph concerning her. Nor was he at fault when different individuals debated the matter.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0023 }

Hugh was somewhat offended.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0024 }

“Nell, I did not anticipate that you would view the issue in this way,” he remarked rather coldly, standing up and stepping in the direction of the office door. This represented their initial drift toward a disagreement.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0025 }

However, Nell hurried behind him and pulled him back.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0026 }

“Listen, Hugh, you must refrain from 'going off mad.’ Take a seat beside me so I can offer a most gorgeous apology, for my remark was completely out of line. However—oh, if you only understood—”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0027 }

Nell stopped herself at the last second. She came exceedingly close to revealing the secret belonging to Lorna.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0028 }

“Understood the way a female views the matter,” she finished haltingly.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0029 }

“I believe I am aware. Having examined the situation from all perspectives, I have arrived at the inescapable conclusion that I am obligated to inform Lorna of my belief regarding the possibility of Rufus being restored to his former self; at that point, my duty ceases. The decision regarding her subsequent actions will rest entirely with her.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0030 }

“It seems to me you lack the right to place this kind of burden upon her. Her load is already heavy enough. She lacks money—in what way could she pay for an operation like that?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0031 }

“Her decision is what matters,” Hugh insisted with stubbornness.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0032 }

“You state that it is your belief that Rufus is capable of being healed. However, are you CERTAIN about that?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0033 }

“By no means. No person could be certain about that. Lesions of the brain itself might have occurred, and their consequences can never be erased. However, if his memory loss and other impairments result simply from the pressure that particular depressed bone areas exert on the brain centers, as I suspect, he is capable of being healed.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0034 }

“But it is merely a potential outcome!” Nell declared. “Now, imagine you inform Lorna and she chooses to undergo the surgery. The expense will be huge. She will be forced to take out a loan, or dispose of her small holdings. And imagine the surgery fails and Rufus does not change.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0035 }

“In what way can she return the funds she takes on credit, or earn a livelihood for her own sake and that huge dependent being if the property is sold?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0036 }

“Oh, I am aware—I am aware. However, informing her remains my obligation. That belief is something I cannot escape.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0037 }

“Oh, the stubbornness of the Carrows is familiar to me,” Nell groaned. “However, you should not undertake this entirely on your own authority. Seek advice from Doctor Dave.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0038 }

“I HAVE done so,” Hugh admitted with hesitation.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0039 }

“And what was his reply?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0040 }

“To put it shortly—like you mentioned—do not disturb what is already fine. Besides his bias opposing modern surgical techniques, I fear he views the situation from your perspective—refrain from doing it, for the sake of Lorna.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0041 }

“There now,” Nell exclaimed victoriously. “Hugh, I truly believe you must defer to the verdict of a person almost eighty years old, one who has witnessed so much and personally rescued dozens of individuals—without question, what he thinks should carry greater weight than the thoughts of a simple boy.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0042 }

“I appreciate it.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0043 }

“Do not laugh. The situation is far too serious.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0044 }

“My point is precisely that. It IS serious. Present here is a man who constitutes an incapacitated burden. Reason and usefulness may be restored to him—”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0045 }

“In the past, he proved immensely helpful,” Nell remarked with scathing sarcasm.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0046 }

“A opportunity to prove himself and make amends for his previous actions might be granted to him. Knowledge of this is kept from his wife. I possess this information. Consequently, informing her about the existence of this chance is required of me. That, in essence, constitutes my choice.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0047 }

“Delay making a 'decision’ for now, Hugh. Get another opinion. See what Captain Saul thinks regarding it.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0048 }

“All right. However, Nell, I will not commit to following what he thinks.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0049 }

“A person has to make this choice on their own. I could not have a clear conscience if I remained quiet about the matter.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0050 }

“Oh, your conscience!” groaned Nell. “Uncle Dave has a conscience as well, doesn’t he, I suppose?”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0051 }

“Yes. However, his conscience is not mine to keep. Come, Nell, were Lorna not involved in this matter—if the situation were entirely abstract, you would be of one mind with me,—you are aware you would.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0052 }

“I would not,” pledged Nell, attempting to convince herself as well. “Oh, Hugh, you may debate throughout the entire night, yet you will not persuade me. Simply query Miss Winifred regarding her opinion on the matter.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0053 }

“When you summon Miss Winifred to reinforce your point, Nell, you have resorted to your ultimate defense. 'Just like a man,’ she will remark, while venting her intense anger. It does not matter. Miss Winifred has no business settling this matter. The decision rests solely with Lorna.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0054 }

“You are well aware of the way she is going to choose,” Nell said, nearly weeping. “She possesses standards of obligation as well. It is beyond me how you are able to assume that kind of burden yourself. I would be unable to.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0055 }

“'For following the right because it is right would be wise even if one disregards the outcome,'”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0056 }

quoted Hugh.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0057 }

“Oh, you consider two lines of verse to be a persuasive piece of reasoning!” Nell mocked. “Such behavior is typical of a man.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0058 }

And after that, a laugh escaped her against her own will. The sound mirrored Miss Winifred so closely.
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0059 }

“Well, provided you refuse to take Tennyson as a reliable source, maybe you’ll trust what is spoken by a Greater than he,” Hugh declared gravely. “'Ye shall know the truth and the truth shall make you free.’ That is something I believe, Nell, using every bit of my heart. In the Bible—or across all literature—no verse is greater or grander, and it is the TRUEST, assuming trueness possesses comparative degrees. Furthermore, speaking the truth, precisely as he perceives and trusts it, constitutes a man's primary obligation.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0060 }

“The truth, under these circumstances, will not liberate poor Lorna,” Nell sighed. “Her bondage will likely become even more bitter as a result. Oh, Hugh, I CAN’T believe you are correct.”
{: #nw-v04-c29-p0061 }
